holidays.name: National Hard Candy Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating all things crunchy, sugary, and slow-dissolving. Think candy canes, butterscotch discs, lollipops, and peppermints. Pop one in your mouth, resist the urge to crunch, and make it last.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a December favorite because it lands in peak candy-cane season.
holidays.funFact: Hard candy is made by boiling sugar syrup to the 'hard crack' stage, about 300°F (150°C). At that temperature it sets into a glassy, non-crystalline solid, which is basically edible glass.

holidays.name: National Oatmeal Muffin Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble oatmeal muffin, the hearty breakfast treat that lets you feel virtuous while eating cake-adjacent baked goods. Bake a batch with raisins, apples, or chocolate chips, or grab one with your coffee.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the run of holiday baking season.
holidays.funFact: Oats were once considered fit mainly for horses in parts of Europe. Today they are a breakfast staple, and muffins let them pass as a treat.

holidays.name: National Emo Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of emo music and culture to break out the black band tees, skinny jeans, and well-worn playlists. It's a chance to sing loudly about your feelings with fellow fans.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial pop culture observance of unclear origin, celebrated by fans of the emo scene.
holidays.funFact: Emo grew out of the mid-1980s Washington, D.C. hardcore punk scene, where it was first called 'emotive hardcore.'
